- **Different, or nothing remembered** — a genuinely new session. Clear all six
  markers, then record the new id.
- **Equal** — the same session re-firing. Keep everything.
- **`session_id` absent, unreadable, or no `jq`** — clear unconditionally and
  drop the remembered id. This is exactly the behaviour the hook had before, so
  a payload shape this repository has not captured cannot make the gate more
  permissive than it already was.

`.session-id` is deliberately excluded from the list it guards: it is the memory
the comparison reads, and clearing it would make every `SessionStart` look new.
It is added to `.gitignore` in the same change — per ADR-0022, an un-ignored
marker enters the working-tree hash, so writing it would move the value the
pairing is about to compare against and no pass could ever stamp.

`session_id` is read from the payload rather than trusted from documentation,
and `scripts/test-review-gate.py` drives the real hook across both branches:
an unseen id clears and records, the same id keeps, a different id clears and
re-records, an absent id clears and forgets. One case fires a `SessionStart`
*mid-cycle* — between the finder finishing and the verifier being dispatched,
the only point at which "keeps them as one block" is observable, because the
verifier's stop consumes the pairing markers — and asserts the pass still stamps.

## Alternatives considered

- **Filter on the payload's `source` field** (`startup` / `resume` / …): rejected
  for now. It may well be the better key, but no real payload has been captured
  here, and choosing a discriminator whose values are unknown would repeat the
  fault ADR-0022 records — describing hook behaviour from documentation rather
  than from an observed payload.
- **Stop clearing review markers at `SessionStart` and rely on the pairing hash
  alone**: rejected. The pairing proves the parent did not edit between the two
  agents; it says nothing about how much later the stamp is spent. Removing the
  clear entirely widens the same hole further than this does.
- **Revert and accept the cost**: rejected after weighing it. The cost is not a
  slow gate, it is a gate that could not be passed at all in this environment.

## Consequences

- A stamp now survives a reconnect-driven `SessionStart`, which is the whole
  point. The fix was confirmed live: the first `SessionStart` after it landed
  reported `gate markers kept`.
- **Accepted residual risk, in the unsafe direction.** `pre-bash-guard.sh`
  authorises a commit on `.review-stamp` merely existing, and ADR-0019 already
  stopped edits from clearing it, so this clear was the last backstop against a
  stamp earned in one context authorising a commit in an unrelated one. It was
  unconditional; now `session_id` equality is the only discriminator. Two ways
  that loses: an id reused after the tree changed out of band (`/resume`, a
  restored container snapshot), and two concurrent sessions sharing one
  `.claude/` directory, where the second to fire reads the first's id. Neither is
  checkable from inside this repository — the payload's uniqueness and lifetime
  are the platform's to guarantee. Before leaning on this mechanism further,
  settle it against the `SessionStart` payload documentation.
- **A third case, failing safe.** The clear and the record are two filesystem
  steps, not one. A hook killed between them leaves the id unwritten, so the next
  same-session fire clears again for nothing — the old cost, once. Reordering
  would invert it rather than fix it: recording first lets an interrupted run
  skip a clear it owed, which is the unsafe direction. A temp-file-and-rename
  makes the write atomic but does not join it to the clear, so the race narrows
  and does not close. Left as is deliberately.
- The hook is no longer a straight-line `rm -f`. Its degraded path is now the
  thing to keep honest: if the fail-safe branch ever stops clearing, the gate
  silently weakens instead of loudly blocking, which is the failure direction
  ADR-0013 cares about. That is what the absent-id test case pins.

documents.title: Session Marker Clear Also Keys On Source
documents.content:
# 0028. The marker clear also keys on `source`, which `/clear` made necessary

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-08-04

## Context

ADR-0027 made `session-start-env-check.sh` clear the gate markers only when
`session_id` changed. It considered keying on the payload's `source` field and
rejected it *for now*, on the grounds that the field's values were unknown and
choosing a discriminator from documentation rather than an observed payload is
the fault ADR-0022 records. It closed by naming the follow-up: settle it against
the `SessionStart` payload documentation before leaning on the mechanism further.

That search has now been done. `source` carries one of five documented values —
`startup`, `resume`, `clear`, `compact`, `fork`. Two consequences fall out, and
the second is the reason this ADR exists rather than a note on the first.

**The resume risk ADR-0027 accepted looked addressable, and is not.** It named id
reuse after an out-of-band change (`/resume`, a restored snapshot) as an unsafe-
direction risk it could not check, and `resume` is one of the five values, so the
first draft of this decision forced a clear on it. That draft cost a stamp within
minutes of landing. `resume` is observed firing inside continuous work in this
environment — one logged instance carried an id that matched the remembered one —
and that single occurrence was enough: treating it as a task boundary reinstates
the treadmill ADR-0027 exists to stop. How often it recurs is unmeasured and does
not need to be. The value being available did not make it the right discriminator.

**ADR-0027 opened a hole nobody caught, including its own review.** `/clear`
resets the conversation — a different body of work starts. Five review passes
over that change never asked what happens if `session_id` survives `/clear`: the
markers would be kept, and an unreviewed task could spend the previous task's
stamp. That is precisely the exposure ADR-0019's stamp-consume rule exists to
police, reopened from a new direction. Whether `session_id` actually persists
across `/clear` is *not* documented — so this is an unbounded risk, not a
demonstrated bug, and it is cheaper to close than to establish.

## Decision

`source` becomes an **additional** clear-trigger, not a replacement. The markers
are kept only when the id matches **and** `source` is not `clear` or `fork` — the
two that begin a different body of work whatever the id says. `resume` is
excluded for the measured reason above; `compact` and `startup` never forced a
clear.

Replacement was rejected deliberately. Which `source` an MCP reconnect reports is
still unobserved; if it reports `startup`, keying on `source` alone would undo
ADR-0027 entirely and restore the bug that cost three passes. Adding a trigger
cannot do that — the change is strictly in the safe direction.

The fail-safe rule from ADR-0027 extends unchanged: an absent or unrecognised
`source` is never a reason to keep. Only the two listed values force a clear;
everything else falls through to the id check, which itself falls through to an
unconditional clear when the id is missing. `scripts/test-review-gate.py` pins
all of it against the real hook — each of the two forcing a clear on the
keep-branch's exact precondition (same id, stamp earned), `compact` and `startup`
keeping, and an unknown value falling back to the id check rather than to "keep".

## Alternatives considered

- **Replace the id check with `source`**: rejected, above. It is the more elegant
  key and may become the right one, but only after somebody observes what a
  reconnect reports.
- **Leave it and record the `/clear` hole as accepted risk**: rejected. ADR-0027
  already carries two accepted unsafe-direction risks; adding a third that is
  cheap to close would be using the residual-risk section as a place to put
  things rather than a place to declare them.
- **Establish first whether `session_id` survives `/clear`, then decide**:
  rejected as sequencing. The observation is worth having, but the fix does not
  depend on its outcome — forcing a clear on `clear` is correct either way, and
  waiting leaves the hole open meanwhile.

## Consequences

- Amends ADR-0027, whose Decision now reads as the id half of a two-part rule.
  Its accepted-risk list is unchanged — the `resume` entry survives, for the
  reason in Context — and gains nothing. What it loses is the `/clear` exposure
  it opened without noticing.
- **A stamp does not survive `/clear`** — provided the harness reports
  `source: clear` for it, which is documented and unobserved, exactly as the last
  bullet says of every value here. If a `/clear` lands mid-task with work still to
  commit, the next commit needs a fresh review. That is the intended cost and the
  right side to err on.
- The keep-branch's precondition is now two facts instead of one, so the test
  suite has to state which one each case is exercising. Every new case therefore
  sets both fields explicitly rather than relying on a default.
- **`source`'s values are documentation, not an observed payload** — the standard
  ADR-0027 held itself to and could not meet. The mitigation is that an
  unrecognised value cannot make the gate more permissive, so the cost of the
  documentation being wrong is bounded at "clears more often than needed".

documents.title: Unified Review And Spec Agents
documents.content:
# 0029. Review and spec verification each run as one agent with internal stages

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-08-07

## Context

ADR-0015 made both pipelines flat finder → verifier pairs of depth-1 agents:
`code-reviewer` → `review-verifier` for the pre-commit review, `spec-verifier` →
`spec-checker` for design-time spec checking. Its load-bearing property was
find ≠ verify independence — a fresh, finding-blind context refutes — which
across this project's review history killed roughly a quarter of all candidates.

The expensive part was never the second agent. It was what a *gate* must prove
once there are two dispatches: that the parent did not edit the tree between
them. That single invariant is why `.finder-done`, `.finder-hash`, `.pair-ok`,
`pre-agent-review-pair.sh` and `lib-review-hash.sh` exist, and the record of what
it cost is unusually complete:

- ADR-0022 — the wrong event first (`PostToolUse`, which fires at launch), then
  two wrong sampling windows (each containing one agent's own run, so the agents'
  scratch files voided innocent passes), plus a hook shipped without its
  executable bit. Four review cycles, three of which could not stamp.
- ADR-0027, then ADR-0028 — once four markers had to survive across a session
  boundary but not across a task boundary, *when to clear them* became its own
  decision, revised twice within one day. Both exist to police a marker set that
  three of four entries only ever served the pairing check.
- `review-diff` step 0 — a paragraph of unresolved observation about
  `run_in_background`, most of which is about a **pair** of dispatches arriving as
  two turns rather than one block.

The repository owner asked for one agent per pipeline, with the stages kept
inside it, and for a simpler stamp. The shape is taken from a fork of this
template that made the same change on 2026-08-07 and could not discharge its
evaluation obligation; see the last consequence.

## Decision

**One agent per pipeline, stages internal.**

- Review: `code-reviewer` alone (`model: sonnet`). Stage A find across all
  lenses, coverage-first → B dedup by (file, line) → C refute each candidate by
  re-deriving it from the real code → D return survivors with `fix` and
  `acceptance`. ADR-0020's contract is unchanged; ADR-0019's single pass is
  unchanged.
- Spec: `spec-verifier` alone (`model: opus`). Stage A formalize → B hunt →
  C replay each candidate against the machine → D return survivors. Still
  design-time, still no gate, still no auto re-run.
- `review-verifier` and `spec-checker` are deleted.

**The names stay.** ADR-0013, ADR-0015, ADR-0019 and ADR-0022 all name
`code-reviewer`; `pre-agent-review-clear.sh` filters on
`subagent_type == "code-reviewer"` and `.claude/settings.json` matches the same
string. Renaming would point four records at an agent that does not exist — the
reason ADR-0022 kept its own hook filename.

**Stage C cites what it read.** Each verdict carries the `file:line` the stage
re-derived it from, so a refutation that never opened the code is visible in the
output. This is a disclosure, not a guarantee (see Consequences).

**The stamp needs one fact: the review agent finished having reported
something.** `SubagentStop` for `code-reviewer`, plus ADR-0022's non-blank
`last_assistant_message` check — which was one of three facts and is now the
only one, so it carries the whole gate. Deleted with the second dispatch:
`.finder-done`, `.finder-hash`, `.pair-ok`, `pre-agent-review-pair.sh`,
`lib-review-hash.sh`, and one `SubagentStop` matcher. `pre-agent-review-clear.sh`
(stamp cleared at cycle start) and `post-bash-stamp-consume.sh` (ADR-0019's
clean-tree consumption) are untouched.

**ADR-0027 and ADR-0028 survive, applied to one marker.** Their decision — keep
the gate's state only when `session_id` matches *and* `source` is neither `clear`
nor `fork` — is about session boundaries, not about how many markers exist. The
rule is unchanged and its reasoning is untouched; the set it governs drops from
four files to `.review-stamp` alone.

**The stamp hook treats `finder`, `verifier` and no argument alike.** Whether the
harness re-reads `.claude/settings.json` mid-session is not established here, so a
cached registration still passing `verifier` must stamp rather than wedge every
commit. `scripts/test-review-gate.py` pins all three invocations.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep both two-agent pipelines**: rejected by the repository owner, who asked
  for the merge after the independence trade-off was stated.
- **Merge review only, keep the spec pipeline two-staged**: rejected. It leaves
  one discipline with two shapes for no stated reason.
- **Keep two agents but drop the pairing check**: rejected — it pays the cost of
  two dispatches and gives up the property that cost bought.
- **Have the merged agent dispatch a child to verify**: rejected — that is
  exactly the depth-2 joint ADR-0015 removed after it lost verdicts three times.

## Consequences

- **find ≠ verify independence becomes a discipline, not a mechanism.** Stage C
  shares a context with Stage A and can see its reasoning. This is the accepted
  risk of this ADR, and it is the property ADR-0015 rejected "self-verify" to
  protect. The `file:line` citation makes a code-blind refutation visible; it
  does not make one impossible.
- **The stamp is no longer bound to a tree.** With two dispatches, `.finder-hash`
  bound it: a parent edit between them yielded no stamp. With one, a parent that
  edits *while the agent runs* gets a stamp for a tree the agent never read.
  Hashing dispatch → completion cannot close it: ADR-0022 tried both ends and
  each was voided by the agent's own scratch files, because the agent holds
  `Bash`. Stated rather than papered over, as ADR-0019 did with its own residual
  gap. The exposure is narrow — the parent is required to wait on the dispatch,
  not work during it.
- **`review-diff` step 0 loses its second half.** What it said about the *gate*
  was that the pairing window spans two dispatches and does not narrow with the
  flag; there is no window left to reason about, and the stamp keys on
  `SubagentStop` either way. The unresolved observation about
  `CLAUDE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_TASKS` stays exactly where it is: AGENTS.md's Delegation
  section names step 0 as the one place it is recorded, and moving it would buy
  nothing but a dangling pointer.
- **ADR-0014's eval obligation applies in full**, unlike ADR-0019 which only
  deleted a mode. This changes how findings are judged, which is the most
  load-bearing edit `review-diff` can take. The run gates the change: if the
  merged pipeline loses expected findings, or over-reports on the benign
  fixtures, against `results/2026-07-29-briefing-skeleton.md` and beyond
  single-run noise, this decision is reverted rather than shipped. That baseline
  is comparable because the agent definitions and Steps 1–4 of the skill are
  unchanged since it was measured; only the parent's dispatch prose moved.
- Supersedes ADR-0015's *mechanism* for both pipelines. Amends ADR-0022: its
  pairing half is moot, its `SubagentStop`-not-`PostToolUse` half stands and is
  now the entire gate.
- Two fewer agent definitions, two fewer hook files, one fewer settings matcher,
  three fewer markers — and with them the three `permissions.deny` pairs and the
  `.gitignore` entries those markers required.
- **The fork this shape came from could not run the gating eval, and that is why
  it runs here.** Its eight review fixtures are context-dependent modification
  patches against template files the fork deleted, so `git apply --check` fails on
  all eight; its own record states the obligation is deferred rather than
  discharged. In this repository the same fixtures apply cleanly, and the
  baselines were measured against them. Making the fixtures fork-portable is a
  real and separate problem: rebuilding them re-baselines every fixture, which
  would destroy the comparison this decision is gated on, so it must not be done
  in this change.

documents.title: AGENTS.md Carries Directives Only
documents.content:
# 0030. AGENTS.md carries directives; rationale, procedure and troubleshooting move out

- Status: accepted (amended by 0031)
- Date: 2026-08-07

> **Note (ADR-0031, 2026-08-07):** the Decision item "`.claude/rules/` is not
> extended" no longer holds. The loader bugs it cited did not reproduce on
> Claude Code 2.1.223 in a local sentinel test, and the Aegis process block —
> which this ADR kept in AGENTS.md — moved to `.claude/rules/aegis.md`
> (`alwaysApply: true`), mirrored into `.cursor/rules/` as file-level symlinks.
> Everything else in this ADR stands: directives-only AGENTS.md, the four-kind
> sort, and the removal rule.

## Context

AGENTS.md is the single always-on instruction file (ADR-0008) and had grown to
234 lines / 29 KB, loaded in full into every session. Two sections held 58% of
it: `## Agents` at 9,544 bytes and `## Aegis Process Enforcement` at 7,496.

Most of that weight is not instruction. It is recorded reasoning — why a
decision was made, what was measured, which sentence was written false and
caught in review — plus operational troubleshooting for situations most
sessions never reach. AGENTS.md's own "Instruction documents" rule says to point
at other files rather than restate them, and the file had become its own largest
violation: the "Permission mode" section restates ADR-0004's 2026-07-28
amendment, the "Review" paragraph restates ADR-0029 and the preloaded
`review-diff` skill, and "Aegis adapter templates" restates ADR-0026.

ADR-0008 solved this shape once for a different file set — seven always-on rule
files became condensed AGENTS.md sections — and its 2026-07-25 amendment records
the two that came back, path-scoped rather than always-on.

## Decision

**Content is sorted by kind, and AGENTS.md keeps only one of the four kinds.**

1. **Directives** — what to do, applying whenever they apply — stay in AGENTS.md.
2. **Rationale** — why a decision was made — becomes a pointer to the ADR that
   holds it.
3. **Procedure and troubleshooting** — needed only while carrying a step out, or
   when it has gone wrong — moves to a skill. `write-adr` takes the MADR-lite
   skeleton, the numbering rules and the ~80-line budget; `aegis-ops` takes
   compile troubleshooting and the `compile_miss` payload.
4. **Rules scoped to particular files** are reached through Aegis path edges
   instead of being restated.

**A paragraph is removed only when a live ADR or skill already holds its
content, confirmed by opening that file in the same change.** Where nothing held
it, the content moved first: `permissions.defaultMode: "auto"` being ignored in
project settings was the one fact in the "Permission mode" section that ADR-0004
lacked, and it became an ADR-0004 amendment before AGENTS.md lost it.

**`.claude/rules/` is not extended.** Adding path-scoped rule files for ADR form
and agent configuration was the obvious route and is rejected twice over. Claude
Code has open bugs in that mechanism — rules with `paths:` not loading for
matching files ([#16853](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/16853))
and loading globally regardless of `paths:`
([#16299](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/16299)) — so a MUST
placed there could be silently absent or silently always-on, the "gate silently
off" failure ADR-0013 exists to prevent. Independently, the text needed no new
home: ADR-0004 and ADR-0014 already held it. What was missing was reach.

**Reach is fixed with edges, not copies.** `.claude/agents/**` and
`.claude/settings.json` gain edges to ADR-0004; before this change neither
reached it and its only path edge came from `src/**/*`. AGENTS.md gains an edge
to this ADR. Each passes ADR-0023's reach test.

## Alternatives considered

- **Compress the prose in place and move nothing**: rejected. The conditional
  sections stay in the always-on budget, and a restatement left next to what it
  restates keeps drifting from it.
- **Reduce AGENTS.md to an index of 2–4 line sections**: rejected. Its value is
  that it is read without being sought. A MUST behind a pointer depends on the
  agent choosing to follow the pointer, and this project's recorded failures are
  mostly agents not knowing to look.
- **Keep every war story in AGENTS.md**: rejected as the default, kept as a
  test. A recorded mistake earns always-on weight only where the directive alone
  would not prevent it.

## Consequences

- AGENTS.md drops from 234 lines to roughly 100, and what remains is
  unconditional. Sessions that never write an ADR or hit a failing compile no
  longer carry the instructions for either.
- Rationale now takes one hop. When Aegis is unavailable, the degraded path —
  reading `aegis-share/source/documents/` directly — is what supplies it, which
  AGENTS.md already requires for every consultation.
- The `aegis:start`/`aegis:end` block shrinks, so a `deploy-adapters` run
  destroys less of this project's own text if one happens despite ADR-0026.
- **The failure mode is a pointer to a record that no longer says what the
  pointer claims, and nothing checks that.** The counterweight is the removal
  rule above: the destination was opened as the pointer was written. This is
  weaker than a gate and is accepted as such.
- ADR-0004 gained an amendment as a side effect of an AGENTS.md change rather
  than from a permissions decision. That is the intended direction — a fact
  belongs with the decision it qualifies, not with the file that noticed it.

documents.title: Aegis Process Rules Move To Claude Rules With Cursor Symlinks
documents.content:
# 0031. The Aegis process contract moves to `.claude/rules/aegis.md`, mirrored into `.cursor/rules/` as file-level symlinks

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-08-07

## Context

The repository owner asked for AGENTS.md's core rules and its Aegis process
sections to stop sharing one file, and for the Aegis rules to reach Cursor
sessions. Three sections were Aegis-specific: the Degraded Environments Aegis
bullet, the `deploy-adapters` warning, and the `aegis:start`/`aegis:end`
enforcement block.

Two earlier decisions blocked the obvious moves. ADR-0030 (same day) rejected
extending `.claude/rules/`, citing Claude Code loader bugs
([#16853](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/16853),
[#16299](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/16299)) — a MUST
placed there could be silently absent or silently always-on. ADR-0026 deleted
the `.cursor/` mirror after its copy drifted for three months undetected.

Both premises were re-measured on 2026-08-07:

- **Claude Code 2.1.223, local sentinel test.** Four rule files in a scratch
  project's `.claude/rules/`: `alwaysApply: true` with Cursor-style
  `description`; `alwaysApply: false` + unquoted single-path CSV `paths:`;
  `alwaysApply: false` + both `globs:` and multi-path CSV `paths:`; and the
  quoted YAML-array `paths:` form the issues call broken. A headless run that
  read no files loaded only the `alwaysApply: true` rule; a run that read
  matching files loaded all four. The test was then repeated with the three
  actual rule files this ADR ships (`aegis.md`, `react.md`, `design.md`) copied
  into the scratch project: the no-read run answered from `aegis.md` alone, and
  a run reading a `.tsx` and a `.css` file loaded both scoped rules. The
  silent-failure modes ADR-0030 cited did not reproduce on this version, and
  lazy path-scoping works.
- **Cursor.** It does not read `.claude/rules/` (confirmed by Cursor staff on
  the [forum](https://forum.cursor.com/t/claude-project-level-rules-not-loaded-with-the-include-third-party-toggle-enabled/157087),
  and by this session, where `react.md`/`design.md` were absent from context).
  File-level symlinks placed directly in `.cursor/rules/` are reported working
  by Cursor staff ([repro thread](https://forum.cursor.com/t/rules-in-a-symlinked-subfolder-mdc-are-not-followed-again/152918)) —
  directory symlinks are the flaky case. Not yet measured in this repository;
  it needs a window reload, which the implementing session could not perform.

## Decision

**`.claude/rules/aegis.md` (`alwaysApply: true`) carries the whole Aegis
contract**: the consultation MUST, the writing/answering procedures, the
MCP-absent degraded path, and the `deploy-adapters` warning. AGENTS.md keeps
one-line pointers where the sections stood.

**Every `.claude/rules/` file is mirrored into `.cursor/rules/<name>.mdc` as a
file-level symlink — never a copy.** A symlink cannot drift, which is the
failure ADR-0026 removed; the extension rename is what makes Cursor's loader
accept it. `react.md`/`design.md` carry dual frontmatter — `globs:` +
`alwaysApply: false` for Cursor, unquoted CSV `paths:` for Claude Code — and
both files, as written, were loaded lazily by the repeated sentinel test above.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep everything in AGENTS.md** (the ADR-0030 status quo): rejected by the
  owner after seeing the trade-offs; the mixing itself was the complaint.
- **Regroup within AGENTS.md**: recommended first, declined — same reason.
- **A generator producing `.cursor/rules/` copies from `.claude/rules/`**:
  rejected; it reintroduces a second artifact under a second discipline, the
  ADR-0026 failure with extra machinery.

## Consequences

- This amends ADR-0030's "`.claude/rules/` is not extended" item and
  ADR-0026's deletion of `.cursor/` — copies stay banned, symlinks are not
  copies. The `deploy-adapters` ban stands unchanged.
- The Aegis MUST now depends on Claude Code's rules loader — the risk ADR-0030
  named. It is accepted on the strength of the local measurement, and a loader
  regression would now silence the contract in Claude Code sessions too, not
  only in Cursor. AGENTS.md's pointer is the only always-on trace that would
  reveal the absence.
- Cursor sessions gain the Aegis contract and the path-scoped rules for the
  first time since ADR-0026 — pending the reload-and-verify this session could
  not do. Until verified, treat Cursor loading as reported, not established.
- AGENTS.md no longer contains the `aegis:start`/`aegis:end` markers. What a
  `deploy-adapters` run does to a marker-less AGENTS.md has not been executed
  here; ADR-0026 records it appending a second copy to marker-less `CLAUDE.md`.
